trust_assignments.title: Cancun Fork: Block State Transition and Transaction Processing

external_entities.name: Network Peer
external_entities.rationale: P2P network peers propagating blocks are unauthenticated. Peers can be malicious, compromised, or simply running different software. Block data must be fully validated.
external_entities.validation_required: Full block validation including header consensus rules, transaction execution, and Merkle root verification.

external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
external_entities.rationale: External users or applications submitting transactions via JSON-RPC are completely untrusted. Transactions can contain malicious data, invalid nonces, or insufficient funds.
external_entities.validation_required: Full transaction validation: nonce check, balance verification, sender EOA check, fee structure validation, and blob transaction field checks.

external_entities.name: Beacon Chain
external_entities.rationale: The beacon chain (consensus layer) is authenticated via the Engine API and has cryptographic attestation. However, the execution layer still performs format validation on withdrawals. The trust exists because both layers are part of the same node deployment under the same operator.
external_entities.validation_required: Format validation of withdrawal data. Withdrawal amounts are converted to Wei and credited to accounts.

trust_boundary_edges.security_assumptions: Block data from peers is untrusted. Full consensus validation must occur before state changes are applied.
Transaction data is untrusted. Comprehensive pre-execution validation must pass before execution begins.
Beacon chain withdrawals come from authenticated Engine API. Format validation is performed but data is generally trusted.

trust_assignments.title: EIP-145: Bitwise Shifting Instructions (SHL, SHR, SAR)

coverage_analysis.note: Pure EVM opcode specification with no external entity interactions. SHL/SHR/SAR operate entirely within EVM execution context on stack data.
Internal consensus mechanism specification for difficulty calculation. No external entities - the difficulty bomb delay affects internal block validation based on block number and fork configuration.

external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
external_entities.rationale: External entity submitting transactions with calldata. No authentication - anyone can submit transactions with arbitrary calldata. The gas floor mechanism mitigates data-heavy transaction spam.
external_entities.validation_required: Calldata token counting, gas floor calculation, and gas limit validation against minimum required.

trust_boundary_edges.security_assumptions: Transaction calldata is untrusted. Gas floor calculation ensures data-heavy transactions pay appropriate gas fees to prevent network spam.
